page: Vultr vx1-m-16c-128gb is a memory-optimized server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor contains 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB network-attached volume, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Text processing via Geekbench also scores in the top tier. However, multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core CPU and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, falls into the average category (middle 50%). Memory performance is robust, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the strong tier (top 25%), while raw memory bandwidth read and write operations remain in the average tier.

The hardware profile is cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require extensive local storage, given the 128.0 GB memory capacity paired with dedicated AMD EPYC cores. The main tradeoff is the minimal 1 GB network-attached local storage, requiring external storage solutions for data-heavy applications. This server is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, text processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference, where its top-tier text generation speed for small models can be leveraged.
